newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 18.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.

- Efforts were continuing on Thursday to avert a sectarian conflict in Londonderry on Saturday when the Protestant Apprentice Boys group hopes to parade around the city walls and a Catholic Bogside resident's group plans to hold a counter-demonstration.
- Irish exporters face being banned from using the Channel Tunnel and rail connections to continental markets unless a system for security clearance is introduced within three weeks.
- The Irish pound has fallen back below 101 pence sterling for the first time in 18 months, bringing further relief to exporters and the farming community.

- Thousands of workers could see their earnings fall because of new legislation that would limit the working week to 48 hours, according to Mary Harney, leader of the opposition party, the Progressive Democrats.
- Dublin county councillors on Thursday rezoned 167 acres of farmland and potentially increased its value from a few hundred thousand pounds to an estimated 13 million punts.
- Following five weeks of talks between Irish Life management and the MSF trade union, settlement of the ongoing dispute involving the company's 430 strong sales force appeared no nearer on Thursday.

- As software manufacturer Stream International announced a 10-million-Irish-pound IDA-backed investment plan to generate 300 jobs in Dublin and Kildare by 1998, concern grew on Thursday about the 800 jobs promised a year ago in three plants at U.S. company APC.
